body.estimand_functional: \(R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and \(\liminf_n n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\); for every admissible rational corrected-prior input, the terminating same-input evaluator gives \(L_{n,k,\varepsilon,\delta}\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le n^{-1}\). Equality of the unrestricted second-order value with \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) remains open.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across units. For any fixed corrected permutation-invariant prior, conditioning on the realized allocation count gives the exact uniform orbit experiment and transfers its Bayes risk to arbitrary count mixtures. Uniform asymptotic optimization over all counts is not yet proved.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive-count local and exterior allocations and zero-count boundary faces all remain in the corrected root obligation; none is removed by division or an interior-allocation assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The prior uses an exactly represented compact rational approximation to the Airy longitudinal density and keeps the explicit nonzero transverse response direction orthogonal to the finite-population contrast.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: The advertised allocation-tube theorem is not proved and its former widening longitudinal prior is impossible: an exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison forces the scaled Bayes deficit to grow at least as \(25T/128\), so it diverges along the claimed \(T_n\to\infty\) schedule. The corrected route uses compact rational piecewise-polynomial squares converging to the Airy ground state while retaining the nonzero transverse response measure. What is proved now is the rational Airy approximation, the corrected prior's exact permutation-orbit reduction, a terminating same-input finite-risk interval, the sharp fixed-\(q^\dagger\) second-order value, and the corresponding unrestricted liminf. Uniform local, shell, and zero-face control remains the root open bridge.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and exact finite programs but not a common second-order limit. The former polynomial tube cannot close that gap because its longitudinal first absolute moment grows with its truncation radius. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen and Hull remain two-arm comparators and do not supply the required unequal-three-arm all-count Bayes bridge.
project_justification.niche: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the eight response types, the unequal full-label score, the nonzero transverse coordinate, and \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations must be handled simultaneously. The corrected compact rational Airy family makes each finite prior exactly evaluable without allowing its first moment to diverge.
project_justification.fill: The present verified contribution is an exact obstruction to the former tube, a weighted-\(H^1\) rational Airy approximation, an exact corrected finite prior and all-design orbit reduction, a terminating same-input interval, and the fixed-design second-order benchmark. The flagship fill still requires certified uniform bounds on the corrected posterior risks over the local face, all exterior shells, and every zero-count face; no sharp unrestricted equality is claimed before that proof exists.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C) supply the two-arm scalar Airy benchmark and feedback bounds; the proved fixed-\(q^\dagger\) multiarm benchmark uses those analytic ingredients together with the response-alphabet score. Hull (2026) is also a two-arm unrestricted-design result. The accepted parent supplies first-order risk, the \(n^{-4/3}\) order, finite response-type games, and same-sample certificates, but no cross-sample all-count limit. The corrected three-arm route is therefore positioned as open at its uniform Bayes bridge, not as a completed extension of these comparators. The prospective ACTG 175 motivation concerns a prespecified complete binary-endpoint regimen contrast and is not a reanalysis of censored outcomes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label gap does not determine the asymptotic design comparison. More decisively, the former widening density has \(\mathbb E|X^\dagger|=5T/16\), which yields a scaled Bayes deficit at least \(25T/128+15\varepsilon/256\) and refutes its claimed finite tube-removal limit. Compact rational Airy approximants repair that defect and support exact finite evaluation, but no proof yet bounds the corrected posterior quotients uniformly over \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, distant positive-count shells, and zero-count faces. Consequently equality versus strict second-order loss of the independent \(q^\dagger\) design remains open.
body.honest_scope: All unconditional statements here are confined to the fixed unequal contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) and fixed \(K=3\). The fixed independent allocation has second-order value \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), the unrestricted deficit has at least that lower-limit value, and every fixed rational corrected-prior input has a terminating exact-algebraic risk interval. Existence of the unrestricted limit, a matching all-procedure converse, a cross-sample threshold, and equality or strict loss of \(q^\dagger\) are not proved. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, arbitrary-real computability, or censored-outcome claim is made.
